summary: A daily synthesis of design news, research, workflows, and culture, curated from today’s crawl and the news for rapha inbox.

questions.question: Who designs the system that designs with us?
questions.answer: Teams are moving from prompt craft to explicit review systems that make judgment visible and reusable.
questions.why: Designers now shape the rules around generation, review, and escalation. That turns critique, governance, and authorship into parts of the product experience.

signals.happened: Product teams are documenting model behavior and review thresholds next to interface decisions.
signals.changes: Add decision checkpoints to the design system before automating more production work.
signals.title: Designing review systems for AI-assisted products

signals.happened: A cross-team study found that generated output converges when feedback is not captured as a shared artifact.
signals.changes: Turn critique into reusable criteria instead of leaving it inside individual prompts.
signals.title: A field guide to design decisions

questions.question: What becomes valuable when making gets cheaper?
questions.answer: The scarce work shifts to framing, taste, and knowing when to stop generating.
questions.why: When teams can produce dozens of plausible options, speed stops being a differentiator. The advantage moves to clear constraints and confident selection.

signals.happened: Teams report that exploration is faster, while alignment and selection now consume more of the schedule.
signals.changes: Budget critique time before adding another generation tool.
signals.title: What becomes valuable when making gets cheaper?

signals.happened: Studios are publishing fewer directions despite producing more internal options.
signals.changes: Measure decision quality and reversibility, not the volume of output.
signals.title: Taste is turning into team infrastructure

further: Taste is turning into team infrastructure

questions.question: Can research stay human at machine speed?
questions.answer: Synthetic participants can widen exploration, but lived context remains the source of consequence.
questions.why: Speed is useful for finding hypotheses, not for replacing the people affected by a decision. Teams need a visible boundary between simulation and evidence.

signals.happened: Research teams are using synthetic interviews to pressure-test scripts before meeting real participants.
signals.changes: Use simulation to improve the plan, then validate consequences with people.
signals.title: Can research stay human at machine speed?

signals.happened: Practitioners found that simulated participants flatten organizational and cultural context.
signals.changes: Label synthetic findings as hypotheses in every research readout.
signals.title: Research repositories after abundance

questions.question: How should design culture change?
questions.answer: Teams are rewriting norms around credit, craft, and critique for an AI-augmented era.
questions.why: The strongest teams are making authorship and review visible. Shared standards protect individual judgment while letting new tools accelerate the work.

signals.happened: Studios are documenting how credit, critique, and accountability work in machine-assisted projects.
signals.changes: Write authorship and review norms before the next AI-supported project begins.
signals.title: How should design culture change?

signals.happened: Creative teams are protecting time for discussion as production cycles become shorter.
signals.changes: Treat critique as core infrastructure rather than a final approval step.
signals.title: Authorship after automation
